title: FixingPointSystem realism labels
description: Expected application labels of one capture. The first session rule that matches a session names its intended application, and default labels the sessions that no rule matches.

threshold.description: Conformance threshold per application. The default is 0.99.

default.description: Application of sessions that no rule matches. Without it such sessions stay unlabelled and do not count.

applications.description: Classifier protocol names that count as each application, per classifier. They replace the built in names for that application and classifier.

tls.description: Expected TLS clients. The encryption check samples the sessions whose rule names a tls_profile, decrypts them, and compares the JA4 of each ClientHello with the profile.

profiles.description: Configured client profiles by name, each with the JA4 fingerprint or fingerprints that its ClientHello has.

sample.description: Most sessions that the check samples. The default is 100.

min_decrypted.description: Share of sampled sessions that must decrypt. The default is 1.

content.description: Settings of the content variety check, which reports the duplicate payload ratio and the payload size distribution of each application. The check runs when this section is present.

max_duplicate_ratio.description: Largest share of duplicate payloads that an application may have. The default is 0.01.

ignore_headers.description: HTTP header names, in addition to the built in list, that the check drops before it hashes a message.

sizes.description: Expected payload size distribution per application. The observed median, and the observed coefficient of variation when cv is given, must lie within tolerance of the expected value.

direction.description: Payloads that count. The default is both.

median.description: Expected median payload size in bytes.

cv.description: Expected coefficient of variation, the standard deviation over the mean.

tolerance.description: Allowed relative deviation. The default is 0.25.

structure.description: Scenario files for the session structure check. The check rebuilds the connections of each scenario instance from the capture and compares their count and ordering with the flows, after edges, and spawn edges of the scenario. It runs when this section is present.

file.description: Scenario file, relative to the labels file.

vars.description: Scenario variables that replace the ones of the file, for example a port that the run changed.

match.description: Limits the sessions that this scenario may claim, with the fields of a session rule.

expected_instances.description: Number of instances that the capture must hold. Left open when absent.

max_gap_s.description: A client that is silent for longer than this many seconds opens a new instance with its next connection. No gap splits instances when absent.

tolerance_s.description: Slack in seconds for the ordering comparisons. The default is 0.

temporal.description: Target distributions of the temporal distribution check, which compares the inter arrival times of sessions and the payload sizes with them through the Kolmogorov Smirnov test. The check runs when this section is present.

alpha.description: Significance level of every KS test. A comparison fails when its p value is below it. The default is 0.01.

min_samples.description: Fewest observations that a comparison needs, in each of its samples. A smaller sample reports insufficient data and fails the check. The default is 30.

arrivals.description: Targets for the gaps in seconds between the first packets of consecutive sessions. Parameters have the names of a scenario delay. A Poisson process of r sessions per second is exponential with mean_ms 1000 / r.

overall.description: Target for all sessions of the capture, labelled or not.

applications.description: Target for the sessions of each application.

sizes.description: Targets for the size in bytes of each payload unit, as the content check defines it. An application can have one target per direction, written as a list.

tls_profile.description: Name of a profile of the tls section, for sessions of a TLS client.

empirical.description: An empirical target: a list of values, a file of numbers separated by white space or commas, or a reference capture whose own sessions give the sample. The check runs the two sample test.

direction.description: Payloads that count, for a size target.

sample_file.description: File name relative to the labels file.

pcap.description: Reference capture, relative to the labels file.

labels.description: Labels file of the reference capture, relative to the labels file. Without it the rules of this file label the sessions of the reference.

time_distribution.description: A distribution of times in the vocabulary of a scenario delay: ms alone or with dist constant, exponential with mean_ms, uniform with min_ms and max_ms, lognormal with mu, sigma, and unit (mu is the natural logarithm of the value in the unit), pareto with alpha and scale_ms, or an empirical target in seconds.

tolerance_ms.description: Distance that still counts as equal. The default is 0.

size_distribution.description: A distribution of sizes in bytes, with an optional direction. lognormal takes mu as the natural logarithm of the size in bytes, and pareto takes alpha and scale, the smallest size.

tolerance.description: Distance in bytes that still counts as equal. The default is 0.

ja4.description: A JA4 fingerprint in the form a_b_c.
